case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment's caption.

number_of_accused.reason: Only one accused, the appellant Sham @ Kishor Bhaskarrao Matkari.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is male, referred to as 'he' and as the brother.

accused_age.reason: Judgment states the accused was 28 at the time of the incident; counsel's 38 is a separate claim.

accused_religion.reason: Religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: Judgment states the accused was jobless at the time of the incident.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status is not discussed in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.reason: Judgment says antecedents are unblemished and nothing shows prior criminal activity.

victim_gender.correct_value: Mixed: male and female victims (Manohar, Akhilesh, Vishwesh are male; Meena and Monika are female)
victim_gender.quote: Manohar, his wife Meena, daughter Monika and son Vishwesh were lying in injured condition
victim_gender.reason: Victims include both male and female persons; 'Male' covers only part of them.

victim_age.reason: Victim ages are not given; the value 28 appears to be the accused's age copied across.

victim_caste.reason: Victim caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

victim_religion.reason: Victim religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused is the real brother of the primary victim Manohar.

offence_category.reason: Offences are murder under s.302 and attempted murder under s.307.

statutory_provisions.reason: Convictions were under ss.302 and 307 IPC; s.201 was charged but the accused was acquitted.

weapon.correct_value: No weapon used per the court; however a large stone and a gas cylinder with tube were found near the body
weapon.quote: No weapon much less a dangerous weapon was used in commission of offence.
weapon.reason: Court says no weapon was used, yet a stone and gas cylinder were recovered near the body; 'None mentioned' omits this.

evidence_type.correct_value: Eyewitness (PW-7, PWs 1 and 3), medical, recovery of stone, confession before Executive Magistrate; statement is not a dying declaration
evidence_type.quote: Though the said statement is not a dying declaration
evidence_type.reason: Judgment expressly says the accused's statement is not a dying declaration; eyewitness evidence is also omitted.

confession.reason: The accused's statement to the Executive Magistrate is treated as a confession and relied on.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: High Court's aggravating circumstances (defenceless victims, assault on children, brutality, false story, no third person, accused slept with victims); Supreme Court rejected the premeditation finding
aggravating_circumstances.quote: This shows that the attack by the accused was predetermined, so also premeditated.
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Premeditation was a High Court finding that the Supreme Court rejected, so listing it as established is inaccurate.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No pre-plan, unblemished antecedents, no weapon and not rarest of rare are all raised as mitigating.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted under ss.302 and 307 and imposed life and seven years RI.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court confirmed conviction and enhanced the sentence to death.

final_outcome.reason: Accused stands convicted; conviction was upheld by the Supreme Court.

offence_finally_established.reason: Murder under s.302 IPC is held established beyond reasonable doubt.

imprisonment_type.reason: Final sentence is life imprisonment restored from the trial court.

imprisonment_years.reason: Life imprisonment has no fixed years; the 7-year RI relates to s.307, not the final sentence.

fine_rs.correct_value: Rs.25,000 (s.302, default two years RI) and Rs.1,000 (s.307, default three months RI)
fine_rs.quote: to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/-
fine_rs.reason: Judgment records fines of Rs.25,000 and Rs.1,000; the value null ignores them.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Accused was in the house sleeping with the victims that night and later attacked them; he gave a false story of thieves. The summary should not state the High Court outcome.
neutral_facts.quote: he was sleeping with the other victims in the same house
neutral_facts.reason: Says accused returned to the house at night, contradicting judgment; also reveals High Court outcome and omits the thieves story.

offence_severity.correct_value: Life imprisonment (s.302) and seven years RI (s.307)
offence_severity.quote: sentenced him to imprisonment for life and 7 years RI under the two counts respectively
offence_severity.reason: Death sentence was set aside; s.307 carried seven years RI, not life imprisonment.

attempt_completion.correct_value: Murders completed; attempted murder under s.307 for the two children
attempt_completion.quote: attempting to murder his other nephew and the niece (PW 7)
attempt_completion.reason: Murders were completed, but the s.307 offence was an attempt, so 'Completed' is incomplete.

physical_harm.reason: Three deaths, injuries to two children, and partial burns to the wife are all stated.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Convictions for three murders (s.302) and one attempted murder (s.307); s.201 charge resulted in acquittal
number_of_offences.quote: acquitted him for the offence punishable under Section 201 IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Judgment does not mention five counts; s.307 was a single conviction, not two.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property loss from the offence is established; the claimed theft was part of the accused's false story.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court found no pre-plan or premeditation and that the quarrel arose from a land dispute.

motive.reason: Motive is the land or property dispute between the brothers.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court relies on PW-7, PWs 1 and 3, the accused's statement, doctors' opinion and stone recovery.

witness_credibility.reason: Court says there is no reason to disbelieve PW-7, PWs 1 and 3, and the confession.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Accused was seen coming out with blood-stained hands and clothes, demanded water, gave a false thieves story, and did not raise alarm
post_offence_conduct.quote: the accused demanded water for drinking
post_offence_conduct.reason: Judgment states post-offence conduct including demanding water and giving a false story; 'Not stated' is wrong.

custody_duration.reason: Judgment gives jail since 30.06.2001 and death cell since 03.05.2006.

bail_history.reason: Bail history is not discussed in the judgment.

trial_duration.reason: Value describes sentencing and appeal outcomes, not trial duration; no trial length is given.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for appellant and respondent match the judgment.

investigation_status.reason: Charge-sheet laid before the Judicial Magistrate and committed to Sessions, as stated.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural irregularity is noted in the judgment.

appeal_history.reason: Matches the trial court, High Court, and Supreme Court sequence of outcomes.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State argued death of three persons and injuries to two in one family justified the death penalty
prosecution_argument.quote: in view of death of three persons and causing injuries to two, all in one family, the High Court was justified in awarding capital punishment
prosecution_argument.reason: Recorded State argument concerned the death sentence; the guilt finding is the court's, not the prosecution's argument.

defence_argument.reason: Defence argued no pre-plan, land dispute, sleeping with victims, unblemished antecedents, not rarest of rare.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Court applied the rarest of rare principle weighing aggravating and mitigating circumstances.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Lists Bachan Singh, Machhi Singh, C. Muniappan, and Ajitsingh Gujral as cited in the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.reason: High Court's death sentence lacked adequate reasons and the case was not rarest of rare.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Court relied on no pre-plan, unblemished antecedents, jobless status, long custody, and reformability.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: These were the High Court's aggravating circumstances, which the Supreme Court held did not justify death
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: The assault on victims by the respondent was aimed at midnight when the victims were fast asleep
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: These were High Court findings the Supreme Court rejected as inadequate, not the Court's own aggravating factors.

other_sentence_order.reason: No other sentence order is recorded beyond setting aside death and restoring life.
